npcs.name: Cosmo, Mordicchiatore di Mondi
npcs.temper: A dog. Cosmo cannot speak and does not understand that anyone expects him to. npcReply must be barking and nothing else: 'Woff!', 'Woff woff!', 'WOFF WOFF WOFF!', possibly with a short action in brackets such as (scodinzola) or (inclina la testa). Never a word of Italian or English outside the brackets, never a sentence, never an explanation. Delighted, escalating barks when the object works; a single confused, deflating bark when it does not.

problem.en: Woff woff! (Cosmo circles you twice, drops a thoroughly destroyed sock at your feet, and stares.)
problem.it: Woff woff! (Cosmo ti gira intorno due volte, lascia cadere ai tuoi piedi un calzino ormai distrutto e ti fissa.)

npcs.solutionHint: The object must be a plaything for a dog: something Cosmo can safely carry in his mouth, chew, chase or fetch. Accept a ball, a tennis ball, a bone, a chew toy, a squeaky toy, a rope toy, a frisbee, a stick, a plush toy, and obvious variants of those. Reject everything else. Reject in particular: tools, machines, vehicles and anything with a blade, a motor, a flame or sharp edges (a saw, a circular saw, a drill, a knife, an axe); anything heavy, hot, breakable or dangerous for an animal; care items such as a collar, a lead, a kennel, a bowl, water, a blanket, a brush, a bath, a vet, a walk, training or attention; and food or meals, the bone being the only exception because he can carry and chew it. If the object is not clearly a dog's toy, the answer is no.

npcs.name: Eleonora, Agile Coach
npcs.temper: Warm, quick and practical, the way someone is when they have run a hundred workshops. Thinks in facilitation terms, laughs at the situation rather than panicking about it, but is genuinely under pressure.

problem.en: The box with all the material for my serious game never made it here, and in half an hour I have forty people in that room. They have to build, move and decide something with their own hands — a talk is exactly what this session must not become.
problem.it: La scatola con tutto il materiale del mio serious game non è mai arrivata, e fra mezz'ora ho quaranta persone in quella sala. Devono costruire, spostare e decidere qualcosa con le loro mani: l'unica cosa che questa sessione non deve diventare è una conferenza.

npcs.solutionHint: Anything a facilitator can put in forty pairs of hands to make a workshop work: post-it notes, sticky notes, dice, playing cards, index cards, markers, pens, flip chart paper, a whiteboard, Lego or building bricks, string, coloured tokens, counters, a timer, a bell, paper to fold, small objects to move around a table. Accept combinations of these. Do NOT accept anything that turns the session back into a talk or replaces the participants' hands: slides, a projector, a PDF, a screen, a lecture, a video, a speaker, a microphone, a laptop for her, or more chairs.

npcs.name: Maurizio
npcs.temper: An organiser running on coffee and adrenaline, checking the time every few seconds. Speaks in short bursts, friendly but visibly doing four things at once.

problem.en: Every talk is overrunning. From the back of the room I cannot tell a speaker their time is up without walking on stage and embarrassing them, and by the afternoon we will be forty minutes behind. I need a way to tell them how long is left, from where I am standing, while they are speaking.
problem.it: Ogni talk sfora. Dal fondo della sala non riesco a dire a chi parla che il tempo è finito senza salire sul palco e metterlo in imbarazzo, e di questo passo nel pomeriggio siamo indietro di quaranta minuti. Mi serve un modo per dirgli quanto tempo resta, da dove sono io, mentre sta parlando.

npcs.solutionHint: Anything that silently tells a speaker on stage how much time is left, visible to them from the room: cards or signs showing the remaining minutes, a large countdown clock or timer facing the stage, a countdown on a confidence monitor or a tablet at their feet, a traffic light, a coloured lamp, a gong or a bell to mark the end, an agreed hand signal. Accept anything a speaker can see or hear from the stage. Do NOT accept anything only Maurizio can see (his own watch, his own phone, a clock at the back of the room facing the audience), anything that requires interrupting them out loud, a longer schedule, fewer talks, shorter slots, or simply asking speakers to be brief.

npcs.name: Paolo
npcs.temper: Calm and dryly funny, the organiser who has already accepted that something will go wrong and is simply deciding which thing. Understates everything.

problem.en: We have two tracks running at once and nothing in this building says which talk is where. People walk into the wrong room, realise after ten minutes, and walk out through the middle of someone's talk. I need them to be able to work out where to go by themselves, at any moment, without asking me.
problem.it: Abbiamo due track in parallelo e in tutto l'edificio non c'è niente che dica quale talk è dove. La gente entra nella sala sbagliata, se ne accorge dopo dieci minuti ed esce in mezzo al talk di qualcun altro. Voglio che possano capire da soli dove andare, in qualsiasi momento, senza chiedere a me.

npcs.solutionHint: Anything that lets an attendee work out where a talk is, on their own, at any time: signs, signposts, arrows on the floor, a printed programme at the door of each room, a large map or schedule board in the hall, room names or numbers on the doors, a colour per track, badges or lanyards coloured by track, a QR code or an app showing the schedule, volunteers stationed at the junctions to direct people. Do NOT accept anything that only works once or only reaches people who are already in the right place: an announcement from the stage, an email sent that morning, a mention in the opening keynote, a page buried on the website, merging the two tracks, or Paolo answering each person himself.
